evidence: STRUCTURE (supports a graded, discriminating reward; no structural defect found). tests/scoring.toml:1-11 gates render/constraints = 0.0, weights functional 0.6 / polish 0.2 / visual 0.2, floor functional 0.05; tests/tools/score.py is byte-identical to the frozen template's and computes reward = weighted mean of the three scored dimensions when gates pass and functional > 0.05 (score.py:40-48). Parsed with tomllib: scored/functional has 43 binary criteria, weighted_mean, weights 0.5-2.5, total 58.5 (largest single row 2.5 = 4.3% of Functional); scored/polish 5 binary criteria, weighted_mean, weights 1.5-3 (total 12); scored/visual 5 likert points=5 criteria with described 1-5 anchors, weight 1.2 each. Only the two gates are all_pass/binary, and they are deliberately cheap prerequisites (sign-in + shared job/candidate). The floor cliff is small: a CRUD-only app passing hro_job_open 0.5 + hro_add_candidate 0.5 + hro_add_email_rules 1 + hro_move_one_stage 1.5 = 3.5/58.5 = 0.060 clears the 0.05 floor. Precondition-collapse is explicitly guarded: scored/functional/prompt.md:13 'Once it succeeds, score EACH criterion independently, continue after failures ... Shared protocols reduce setup; they are not conjunctive bundles. When a setup step fails, set up the same thing again on a new job of your own'; prompt.md:23 'Never deduct one observed defect in more than one row'; polish/prompt.md has the equivalent independent-judging line. Reasoned spread: (a) a non-realtime but otherwise complete app loses hro_live_board 2.5, hro_msg_exchange 1.5, hro_unread_counts 2, hro_unread_scrolled_up 2, hro_seen 1.5 (9.5/58.5) and the two live polish rows (6/12) -> about 0.6*0.84+0.2*0.5+0.2*v, well below the golden but far above zero; (b) a board-only app with no conversations loses ~T/U/K rows (~20/58.5) and most polish -> mid-range; (c) a role-less app (no server-side permission checks) loses hro_mgr_*, hro_observer_readonly, hro_candidate_no_staff, hro_anonymous, hro_candidate_private (~10.5) -> mid-high. Each produces a distinct partial score, not 0/1. MEASUREMENT (absent). raw-evidence-index.json 'scope' states verbatim: 'Full configured grading/workload, reward discrimination/ranking and Oracle/target scores are absent.' The six indexed artifacts (hashes verified) are scripted golden browser/API observations of the reference only; there is no run of mutated/weak apps through the configured judges, so the actual spread produced by the claude-code judge on partial apps is unmeasured. Per REVIEW_POLICY.md ('separate, hash-bound runtime records for ... reward discrimination') and SKILL.md ('Never upgrade an unmeasured claim to Pass'), this row cannot be cleared. Residual design observations (not defects): every functional/polish row is strict conjunctive binary ('Fails if any condition stated above does not hold'), so a nearly-correct feature scores 0 on its row; with 43 rows this still yields fine granularity. Live-update capability is correlated across 5 functional rows and 2 polish rows (different observables owned per row), so a non-live app is penalised in both dimensions; this is intentional weighting, not collapse. Tried counterexamples: broken app that could pass high - a static/seed-only shell is stopped by the constraints gate (independent-context readback, 'browser-only save' excluded); a conforming alternative that could fail - an app doing mutations over WebSocket instead of fetch could hinder 'replay the captured request' rows, but prompt.md:23 directs replaying 'the closest observed request' and the polish prompt allows replaying 'a request already observed from the UI', so not an all-or-nothing collapse; not exercised at runtime.
suggested_fix: No source change required for this row. To clear it, record a hash-bound reward-discrimination run: score the golden plus 3-4 mutated weak apps (e.g. no live push, no conversations, no server-side role checks, static shell) through the configured gates+scored suites and confirm a monotone spread of distinct rewards between 0 and the golden.
